card.title: Sr. Manager, Assembly, Integration & Test, Project Sunrise - Orbital Data Centers
card.description:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of Advanced Concepts and Enterprise Engineering (ACE), supporting Blue Origin’s mission of millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. The team fosters innovation and drives engineering workflows of the future, shared solutions and standards, simplicity and lower costs, and manufacturable design.

**About the Program**
---------------------

Project Sunrise is designing and building orbital data centers — spacecraft that run AI compute workloads on 100% solar power in orbit. This is a first-of-kind program at the intersection of spacecraft engineering and hyperscale GPU infrastructure, housed within Blue Origin. We are building the team from scratch and need people who can operate at the frontier of both domains.

 

**About the Role**
------------------

his is a leadership role with technical depth: you will manage and develop people, and also own integration and test technical content yourself, alongside senior individual contributors who report to you. You have led spacecraft integration and test through qualification and into production, and you want to do it again with a new kind of payload, a tighter schedule, and a team you get to shape from the start. You will work side by side with Manufacturing, Systems Engineering (verification), the technical leads for the spacecraft bus, compute system, software, and operations. You will represent Assembly, Integration & Test in Program leadership forums and reviews.

 

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

* Build and lead the Assembly, Integration & Test organization: hire and develop integration and test engineers, technicians, and automation and test data specialists, set clear ownership, and scale the team as the program moves from qualification to production

* Own the integration and test schedule and facility resource allocation: sequence qualification and acceptance campaigns, balance competing demands for chambers, shakers, and test benches, and surface schedule risk early

* Own test anomaly resolution: set the process for stopping safely, preserving evidence, finding root cause, and dispositioning nonconformances, and close anomalies with the design and systems teams

* Plan facilities and equipment: define the space, power, cleanroom, environmental test, and ground support equipment needs, and make build, buy, or lease decisions on schedule

* Drive the design the production flow from first-article integration through repeatable acceptance, with defined stations, handoffs, and test gates that Manufacturing and Operations can run

* Drive test automation: set the architecture for electrical ground support and automated test equipment, and deliver more than 80% automated acceptance testing

* Own the test data and digital thread: make sure results are captured, stored, and traceable to requirements, configuration, and hardware serial numbers, and that they flow to engineering, quality, and operations

* Work with Systems Engineering to implement the verification plan: make sure test configurations, procedures, and readiness reviews support requirement closure, and give test feasibility feedback into requirements and design

* Partner with the spacecraft bus, compute system, and software teams so designs can be integrated and tested, building test access, telemetry, and interface needs into the design early

* Manage relationships with suppliers and external test houses: define scope, schedule, and acceptance criteria, and bring the program's integration and test standards to supplier reviews

* Support the production readiness maturity checklist with objective evidence from integration and test

* Set the safety culture on the factory floor and in the test cell, including hazardous operations review and safe handling, and build a team that stops work without hesitation when something looks wrong

 

**Required Qualifications**
---------------------------

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, physics, or a related technical field; master's degree preferred

* 12+ years of spacecraft integration and test, or comparably complex hardware test, experience, including ownership of spacecraft-level qualification or acceptance testing

* Prior experience leading and developing engineers and technicians as a manager, lead, or chief test engineer

* Demonstrated experience running a test schedule and test facilities for flight hardware, including environmental test (vibration, thermal vacuum, EMI/EMC) and the resource trade-offs that come with it

* Experience resolving test anomalies and nonconformances on flight hardware through root cause and closure

* Experience with test automation, including electrical ground support equipment and automated test equipment, and with test data management and traceability

* Experience establishing or substantially improving integration and test processes, facilities, or tools in a fast-moving environment

* Ability to make and defend sound technical decisions with incomplete information, and to communicate clearly with engineers, executives, suppliers, and customers

 

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

* Experience taking a spacecraft from first-article integration to production-rate acceptance testing, including converting manual procedures to automated test

* Experience with high-power or high-heat-flux spacecraft, or with high-density electronics, HPC, or GPU hardware in demanding environments

* Experience planning and commissioning new test facilities or major environmental test equipment

* Experience managing external test houses or test suppliers, including scope, schedule, and quality oversight

* Hands-on experience with digital engineering and manufacturing execution or test data systems, including linking test results to configuration and requirements

* Experience on commercial or rapid-development programs, and judgment in tailoring heritage standards to what a program actually needs

* Experience supporting launch site operations or on-orbit commissioning

 

**Additional Information**
--------------------------

* U.S. citizenship or permanent residency required (ITAR)

* Travel may be required up to 15% of the time but may change based on project needs.

* Relocation assistance available.

 

Base Pay Range for:

VA applicants is $171,093.00 - $239,529.15
CO applicants is $157,318.00 - $220,244.85
WA applicants is $171,093.00 - $239,529.15

**Other site ranges may differ**

 

**Culture Statement**

Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

 

**Export Control Regulations**

Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

 

**Background Check**

* Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical 

 

**Benefits**

* Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
* Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
* Paid Time Off: Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details. 

 

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. We provide all qualified applicants for employment and employees with equal opportunities for hire, promotion, and other terms and conditions of employment, regardless of their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin/ethnicity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local law. Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws.

 

**Affirmative Action and Disability Accommodation**

Applicants wishing to receive information on Blue Origin’s Affirmative Action Plans, or applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the application and/or interview process, please contact us at EEOCompliance@blueorigin.com . Please note this is a publicly managed inbox. Please do not include any personal medical information in your request.

card.title: Director, Operational Excellence
card.description:
* Team:Industrial Operations & Product Supply
* Location:Saratoga Springs
* Req ID:R53235
* Contract:Full time
* Work Pattern:Onsite

**The role**
------------

**Build our future together:**

At Regeneron, we use science and innovation to develop life-changing medicines for people with serious diseases. We’re hiring an Associate Director/Director of Operational Excellence for our highly automated bulk/ drug substance manufacturing plant, supporting 20–30 tech transfers a year alongside commercial delivery responsibility. GMP production will run concurrently with construction and CQV for 3–5 years. This role requires both building and operating.

 
 

This site operates on a foundation of strategy, execution, and discipline. Every function at the site owns a pyramid of metrics derived from annual goal planning that connects the site’s strategic goals to the factory floor, with performance measured back up to leadership to monitor, track, and mitigate against contingencies quantified using SMART goals in days and dollars.

 
 

The Associate Director/Director of Operational Excellence runs our site MDI (managing for daily improvements) OpEx, continuous improvement programs, and all site PMO operations owning the site project register and deciding how work is staffed and prioritized across the project portfolio while coordinating cross-functional projects. They build the operating rhythm that turns discrete functions into one aligned site team as the site scales to six suites, and owns the site’s strategy, execution, and culture discipline planning. Lead executive-level investigations and special initiatives as project/program lead, absorbing crisis response so operational leaders can stay focused on daily management.

 
 

**When & where:**

* Location: Saratoga Springs, New York, United States

* Work model: Monday-Friday, 8am-4:30pm
 

 

**Discover your role:**

* Run site MDI including ownership of the Tier 6 site critical issue forum, ensuring cross-functional blockers are surfaced and resolved quickly

* Establish and sustain the site's cadence of daily, weekly, and monthly forums so issues are raised and resolved at the right level

* Lead OpEx and continuous improvement programs, building and prioritizing a CI project pipeline and delivering realized savings

* Lead all site PMO activities, owning the site project register and deciding how work is staffed and prioritized across the project portfolio, coordinating cross-functional projects and site initiatives and driving on-time delivery

* Own site strategy, execution, and rigor planning for culture translating strategic priorities into a disciplined, trackable execution plan across the site

* Own MDI and all standard work initiatives site-wide, ensuring consistent methodology and application across every function and suite

* Own site-wide implementation of lean principles building and driving the phased adoption roadmap across leadership, suites, and functions, from initial leadership alignment through daily floor-level practice

* Own site business analytics building and maintaining the reporting, dashboards, and KPI infrastructure that drive MDI, CI prioritization, and Site Leadership Team decision-making

* Co-lead the monthly finance/business review with finance operations, reconciling cost and capital needs against the site's financial plan

* Coach leaders and teams in Lean and problem-solving methods and build an OpEx culture across the site

* Embed MDI and OpEx practices as suites come online so new suites start up with the site's operating standards

* Partner with manufacturing, quality, technical services, technical operations, supply chain, and Finance as a member of the site leadership team

* Embed the digital and connected plant model in site MDI, using real-time data and digital tools for daily management and escalation

* Own the site's multi-year operational efficiency roadmap, driving leaner operations and delivering year-over-year efficiency gains

* Build, coach, and retain a high-performing OpEx team; establish high standards for performance management and accountability; perform other duties as required

* Own a gross margin improvement program and goal for this function, contributing to the site's overall margin performance

* Ensure this function's metrics flow up and down through the MDI structure, connecting into the site's S&OP, AOP, and long-range planning cycles

* Own these function's OpEx and CapEx budget and roadmap

* Serve as the primary party responsible for this function's alignment with the Global Center of Excellence (COE), connecting site execution back to the business-level function
 

 

**This role requires:**

* B.S in engineering, life sciences, business or related technical field
* MBA & PMP certification preferred

* + Associate Director: 10+ years of operational excellence, continuous improvement, or manufacturing operations or biopharmaceuticals including 5+ years of progressive leadership

* + Director: 12+ years in operational excellence, continuous improvement, or manufacturing operations or biopharmaceuticals including 7+ years of progressive leadership

* + Level will be determined based on experience

* Previous people leadership/supervisory experience

Does this sound like you? Apply now to take your first step towards living the Regeneron Way! We are committed to building a workplace with an inclusive culture. Regeneron is an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion or belief (or lack thereof), sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, gender reassignment, marital or civil partnership status, civil status, pregnancy or parental status, age, disability, nationality, citizenship status, ethnic or national origin, membership of the Traveler community, familial status, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected under applicable law. Where required, we will provide reasonable accommodation to applicants with known disabilities or chronic illnesses during the recruitment process, unless such accommodation would impose undue hardship.

Where necessary, we disclose salary ranges for roles in all countries in which we operate. The final offer will be determined within the relevant range based on the country of employment, specific role level, and your skills and experience. In some countries, collective bargaining agreements (CBAs) may apply and influence certain elements of pay or benefits. Regeneron offers a competitive and comprehensive total rewards package which may include, depending on country and role: annual bonuses or other incentive plans, equity awards, pension or retirement benefits, 401(k) company match, health and wellness programs, fitness centers, insurance benefits (e.g. medical, dental, vision, life and disability), paid time off, and family support benefits. For additional information about Regeneron benefits in the U.S., please visit https://careers.regeneron.com/en/working-at-regeneron/total-rewards/. For other locations, additional information will be provided during the recruitment process. If you have any questions, please speak with your recruiter.

 
 

Please be advised that at Regeneron, we believe we do our best work when we are together. For that reason, many roles are required to be performed on‑site. Please speak with your recruiter and hiring manager for more information about on‑site expectations for your role and location.

 
 

As part of the recruitment process, certain background checks may be conducted in accordance with the laws of the country where the position is based. The purpose of such checks is to verify certain information prior to the commencement of employment such as identity, right to work and educational qualifications.

 
 

For jobs in Canada: this posting is for an existing position.

 
 

**Salary Range (annually)**

$150,800.00 - $292,700.00

card.title: Senior Director, Brand Strategy - PFG Manufacturing
card.description:
**Job Description:**

**We Deliver the Goods:**

* Competitive pay and benefits, including Day 1 Health & Wellness Benefits, Employee Stock Purchase Plan, 401K Employer Matching, Education Assistance, Paid Time Off, and much more
* Growth opportunities performing essential work to support America’s food distribution system
* Safe and inclusive working environment, including culture of rewards, recognition, and respect

**Position Purpose** 
 
The Sr Director, PFG Manufacturing Brand Strategy owns and is accountable for Manufacturing brand strategies, growth initiatives, and works with the Vice President of Sales to shape the Division’s commercial strategy. This role leads the development and execution of long-range brand strategies that support Manufacturing revenue, margin, customer growth, market expansion, and business performance objectives. The position partners with Sales, Operations, Finance, Marketing, and Manufacturing leadership to establish commercial priorities, align customer commitments with production capabilities, evaluate market opportunities, and drive strategies that strengthen customer relationships and profitable growth. This role provides strategic direction, decision support through insights, and executive-level leadership to guide commercial planning, brand awareness, pricing strategy, demand planning, and long-term business performance. 
 
**Major Functional Responsibilities**

* Leads the development and execution of brand strategies that support Manufacturing revenue, margin, customer growth, and market expansion objectives.
* Partners with Manufacturing, Operations, Finance, Marketing, and Sales leadership to align sales plans, customer commitments, pricing actions, and production capabilities.
* Analyzes market trends, customer needs, competitive activity, sales performance, and financial results to identify opportunities, risks, and recommended actions.
* Builds and maintains effective relationships with key customers and internal business partners to support customer retention, growth, and service execution
* Owns pricing governance, promotional strategy, contract opportunity evaluation, customer profitability planning, and revenue optimization initiatives for Manufacturing.
* Identifies new customer, channel, product, and market opportunities that support Manufacturing growth and business strategy.
* Provides direction, coaching, and support to assigned associates and cross-functional resources to ensure priorities, timelines, and deliverables are met.
* Leads executive-level business reviews by presenting commercial strategy, business performance insights, growth priorities, pricing decisions, and recommended actions that guide Manufacturing leadership planning.
* Establishes and monitors sales strategy initiatives, commercial KPIs, pricing performance, growth metrics, and corrective action plans to drive accountability for Manufacturing business results.
* Performs other duties as assigned

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's Degree - Business or related stuty
* 8+ years of progressive experience in brand and commercial strategy, sales operations, commercial planning, business development, using insights to generate actions, revenue planning, or related commercial functions
* Strong knowledge of brand strategy, commercial planning, data insights, customer planning, and business performance analysis.
* Ability to analyze market, customer, financial, and operational data and translate findings into practical business recommendations.
* Ability to partner effectively with sales, operations, manufacturing, finance, marketing, and leadership teams.
* Ability to lead projects, influence stakeholders, manage competing priorities, and deliver results in a fast-paced business environment.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office, CRM tools, sales reporting systems, financial analysis tools, and related business applications.
* Strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to prepare and present information to leadership and business partners.
* Works on complex business issues involving sales performance, customer needs, pricing, margin, and market conditions. Problems require analysis, cross-functional input, and practical recommendations. Problem/task resolution timeframe is typically three to twelve months.
* Works under general direction. Exercises judgment within established policies, practices, and business objectives. Receives guidance on overall priorities and strategic direction from the Manufacturing VP, Sales & Marketing.
* Decisions and recommendations may impact revenue growth, margin performance, customer relationships, production planning, service execution, and Manufacturing business results.
* Regularly interacts with Sales, Operations, Finance, Marketing, Manufacturing, and executive leadership. May interact with customers, suppliers, and external business partners related to sales strategy and growth initiatives.
* Supports sales revenue, margin, pricing, forecasting, and customer profitability objectives for Manufacturing. Provides recommendations that influence revenue growth and business performance. Does not have direct P&L ownership unless assigned by business leadership

**Company description**

Start-to-finish manufacturing, packing, and distribution of best-in-class, grab-and-go items to drive growth to a customer’s bottom line — this is the dynamic and delicious world of PFG Manufacturing. With the latest array of in-house manufactured food, snack, and beverage offerings, customers can choose products from a family of name brands or create their own custom-made, private label products to stand out in the market.

**Awards and Accolades**

Performance Food Group and/or its subsidiaries (individually or collectively, the "Company") provides equal employment opportunity (EEO) to all applicants and employees, regardless of race, color, national origin, sex, marital status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, and any other characteristic protected by applicable local, state and federal laws and regulations. Please click on the following links to review: (1) our EEO Policy; (2) the "EEO is the Law" poster and supplement; and (3) the Pay Transparency Policy Statement.

card.description:
Job Description
 
 
The Executive Director, Organization & Talent Partner (OTP), Manufacturing Division, reports to the Vice President, Human Resources, Manufacturing Division and serves as the senior strategic organization and talent advisor to senior leaders and their leadership teams within the Global Biologics Operating Unit and the Global Science Engineering and Commercialization organization.
 
 
Operating with a divisional as well as an enterprise mindset, the leader architects the long-term view that connects priorities and business needs into organizational capability planning solutions that help ensure these organizations have the structures, capabilities, leadership, talent pipelines and ways of working needed to deliver their priorities.
 
 
The role operates across complex scientific, pipeline, workforce, geographic and organizational priorities; co-creates strategy; frames organization and workforce choices; and establishes governance and ways of working across multiple leadership interfaces.
 
 
The Executive Director leads a team of two Organization & Talent Partners. Operating with an enterprise mindset, the role connects priorities across Manufacturing, partnering with Talent Enablement and commissioning the right expertise from Centers of Excellence (COEs), Enterprise Team HR (ETHR) and HR Solutions & Operations to bring strategy into execution. As a people leader, the role is accountable for the direction, development, performance and effective deployment of a direct and indirect team of HR professionals.
 
 
**Primary Responsibilities:** 
Shape the agenda
 
 

* Understand, anticipate and translate business strategy into the long-term organization and talent agenda​
* Lead organization capability planning so structures, roles and capabilities are ready for where the business is going​
* Drive strategic workforce planning linked to business direction and transformation
* Bring an enterprise perspective to leadership and business planning, connecting organization, workforce and talent implications across leadership teams and the broader enterprise.

Develop the organization and its leaders
 
 

* Enable talent development strategy, including succession and leadership development for critical populations​
* Coach senior leaders to improve organizational effectiveness, leadership impact and talent decisions​
* Support transformational efforts from an organization and talent perspective​
* Act as steward in organizational effectiveness, driving stronger collaboration across functions and clarity in interfaces, so priorities connect rather than compete

Leverage the HR operating model to bring strategy into execution
 
 

* Be accountable for the strategy and execution of macro-level organizational change and transformation and ensure the right partnerships are activated to deliver successful execution​.
* Engage with TELs, COEs, ETHR, HR Solutions & Operations and other partners to deliver the highest-value business priorities, leveraging expertise and capacity where they reside. Across these partnerships, provide context on business priorities and dynamics, connect organization and talent priorities across divisions and countries
* Seek to understand local nuances and considerations when defining organization and talent strategy and execution plans​

​
 
 
**Experience, capabilities and leadership characteristics:** 
The successful candidate will bring deep strategic HR experience in a large, complex organization and a record of shaping outcomes through influence. The role requires the following capabilities and leadership characteristics:
 
 

* Business savviness: bring the depth of advanced business understanding needed to build differentiated talent strategies and workforce plans leaders will trust​.
* Organization development and effectiveness: diagnose how well the organization is working and take action to close the gaps and strengthen effectiveness, using the OCP playbook and OD team resources​.
* Talent growth and senior-leader coaching: anticipate talent and capability gaps in critical populations well before they become urgent, and shape the succession and development plans that close them​.
* Influence and executive communication: effectively frame and communicate complex or sensitive issues clearly and confidently to stakeholders and partners to ensure effective action is taken, ​and align senior stakeholders without relying on formal authority.
* Change catalyst leadership: drive the organizational and cultural shifts your strategy requires, championing new approaches and helping people move through resistance to get there​.

card.description:
Description:

**About Us**

Family-owned and operated since 1970, we are an industry-leading gas distributor founded on unparalleled customer service. Our industrial, medical, food, and specialty gas products support a variety of industries that work daily to improve the world we live in, and our ongoing commitment to serve spans the southwestern United States with 16 locations across California and Arizona. Discover the most interesting industry you’ve never heard of!

**Position Overview**

The Plant Manager oversees the daily operations on the plant floor while enhancing production and revenue. You will manage scheduling, supervise daily operating reports, and boost production by providing leadership and developing strategic plans.

**Essential Functions**

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

* Lead, manage, and develop plant employees to ensure they possess the necessary capabilities and culture to maintain effective operations. This includes establishing direction, gaining commitment, delegating responsibilities, and building organizational capabilities
* Ensure all staff members adhere to OSHA general standards related to manufacturing facility safety protocols
* Responsible for maintaining the facility, including understanding and explaining basic mechanical theory to direct reports, coordinating with vendors, and projecting and establishing preventative maintenance programs and schedules while directing the maintenance staff to ensure all equipment is properly maintained and operational
* Workforce Planning/Scheduling
* Ensure our products meet or exceed quality control standards using specified SOP testing methods
* Manage notable projects and improvements as directed
* Create a work environment that ensures the safety and health of employees, the community, and the environment
* Focus on continuously improving the competitiveness of operations
* Recognize customer commitment and drive activities for ongoing quality improvement
* In conjunction with senior group management, establish and oversee activities to meet short- and long-term plant goals
* Improve efficiency and capacity through capital expenditure improvements in processes and procedures and through both formal and informal continuous improvement activities
* Conduct monthly safety meetings as needed
* Other duties as assigned

Requirements:

* 5 years of experience in production management
* Ability to operate or willingness to train for forklift operation
* Production/distribution experience required; industrial gas industry or equivalent experience preferred
* In-depth knowledge of cylinder gases and processes of each
* Knowledge of all regulatory agencies including, but not limited to, FDA, DOT, OSHA, and EPA
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills; ability to communicate effectively with customers, employees, and management
* Ability to lift 50 pounds and stand for extended periods
* Proficient computer skills, including Microsoft applications, TIMS CU

**Supervisory Responsibility**

Manages direct reports

**Physical Demands**

The physical demands described here represent those that an employee must meet to perform the essential functions of this job successfully.

While performing this job, the employee must stand for long periods, talk, hear, and use hands and fingers to operate a computer and telephone, reach, stoop, and kneel. This person must be able to lift, carry, or set down 50+ pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision requirements due to computer work.

**Travel**

No travel is expected for this position

**Position Type and Expected Hours of Work**

This is a full-time, exempt, and on-site position. Typical days and hours of work are Monday through Friday, and range from 6:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

**Compensation and Benefits**

* Individual and company performance-based quarterly bonuses as outlined in our plan documents
* Annual performance-based merits
* Comprehensive benefits package:
 + Medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance
 + Health Savings Account (HSA) and Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
 + Voluntary accident coverage, hospitalization plans, Employee Assistance Programs (EAP’s), Wellness platform access
 + 401(k) + company match
* 7 company-paid holidays
* 3 weeks of paid time off (PTO) earned on an accrual basis
* Professional development opportunities and ongoing training
* Healthy work/life balance and a collaborative and inclusive company culture

The compensation range reflects WestAir’s good-faith estimate for the base compensation expected at the time of posting. Compensation offered will be determined by the job-related factors, including skills, experience, qualifications, education, and geographic location.

This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive. An employee may perform other related duties as negotiated to meet the organization’s ongoing needs.

WestAir Gases and Equipment, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Do you thrive in an environment where meaningful work happens every day? Do you want to make a difference in the lives of older adults?

 

**Mercy Retirement & Care Center** has been at the forefront of senior care for more than 150 years. Situated on our lush campus in Oakland, we provide assisted living, memory care, skilled nursing and rehabilitation services to meet a variety of healthcare needs. We provide exceptional, person-centered care that enhances the quality of life for our residents.

 

Our **Culture of Excellence** is built on a foundation of respect, integrity, and a commitment to the well-being of both our residents and our team members. We foster a collaborative and supportive environment where innovation and compassion drive everything we do.

This position is responsible for the supervision and administration of security services, maintenance operations, and ground management, in addition to overseeing capital improvements. Ensures a secure and welcoming atmosphere for residents, staff, volunteers, and visitors, this position provides management, technical expertise, life safety reviews, and quality assurance initiatives to guarantee customer satisfaction and adherence to regulatory standards related to the physical plant maintenance and appearance as well as a dedication to maintaining our World Class **Culture of Excellence.**

 

**Our Plant Ops Director:**

* Oversees preventative maintenance of systems, buildings, and grounds. Manage contracts with external experts and contractors, as necessary.
* Manages capital projects, which includes handling project bids, selecting and overseeing contractors, and managing purchases and expenditures within the allocated budgets. Ensure that project status reports and related documentation are submitted promptly.
* Supervises maintenance operations, including an organized system for tracking work orders. Promotes the efficient use of resources, with a focus on energy conservation.
* Conducts quality assurance inspections as needed to uphold high service standards. Engages in various Quality Improvement programs and committees, either personally or by designating appropriate facility personnel.
* Actively participates in and supports the Work Safety committee.
* Performs safety reviews of the campus; ensures compliance with regulations concerning buildings, systems, and disaster response protocols.
* Oversee security services for the community.
* Understands the essential role of security, establishes necessary protocols and procedures, and secures personnel to ensure the safety of both residents and team members.
* Develops job descriptions; recruits-hire, trains, schedules, supervises, and advises personnel in relevant departments. Assesses performance, suggests promotions and salary adjustments, and implements progressive disciplinary measures for Plant team members.
* Acts as an integral member of the management team.
* Performs other duties as assigned.
 

 

**What you need to succeed:**

* High School Diploma required; with some college coursework preferred. Contractor’s license is preferred but is not a requirement.
* Minimum of 6 years’ related experience in facilities management, construction, engineering, property management and maintenance, at least 3 years in health care or retirement community environment.
* An advanced understanding of building codes, life safety regulations, and Cal-OSHA standards is required, along with journeyman-level expertise in HVAC/boiler systems, electrical, plumbing, and mechanical equipment.
* Excellent verbal and written communications skills in the English language.
* A valid driver's license is required, along with strong leadership and supervisory skills.
* Familiarity with safety policies and procedures is also essential.
* Committed to delivering high-quality and professional interactions with residents, volunteers, and staff members.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly in Office 365, including Microsoft Word, Excel, and email software, is expected.
* Capable of demonstrating adaptability, informed decisions under pressure, and effectively prioritizing tasks and projects.
* Completion of a background check and drug screening. Pre employment screenings may also include a physical, TB test, and fingerprinting per state/local guidelines.
 

 

**Physical Requirements:**

* May involve lifting, pushing, pulling, up to 75lbs, and transporting equipment, and candidates may encounter challenging environmental conditions, such as dirt, noise, heights, and confined spaces, necessitating caution for safety.
* To ensure the health and safety of both our team members and residents, Elder Care Alliance may mandate that team members receive vaccinations, engage in daily screenings, undergo surveillance testing, and utilize face coverings along with other personal protective equipment (PPE) in accordance with regulatory guidelines to mitigate the transmission of infectious diseases.
* Essential abilities for the safe execution of duties include good vision and hearing; full mobility on steps and ladders; adequate dexterity and mobility in both arms (or mechanical alternatives) to operate hand and power tools, gauges, and valves safely.
* Physical requirements can be accommodated with mechanical aids/devices.

For our client, we are seeking a Director of Manufacturing and Quality to join the team of a leader in the Consumer Technology space.
 
 
This leader will own the global manufacturing strategy and quality execution for a hardware-driven business operating across design, production, and supply chain partners. The role will be central to scaling high-volume manufacturing, improving operational efficiency, and ensuring product quality from early design through full production. You will work closely with engineering, contract manufacturers, and cross-functional partners to strengthen launch readiness, vendor accountability, and long-term quality performance.
 
 
Location: Sunnyvale, CA
 
 
Compensation: $200,000 – $250,000 annually
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Architect and execute the global manufacturing strategy, including optimization of production facilities
* Drive NPI handoffs from design to high-volume manufacturing with robust playbooks
* Optimize production capacity and efficiency through innovative layout and automation designs
* Manage technical execution at tier-1 contract manufacturers and oversee vendor accountability
* Own and improve the global Quality Management System across all sites and partners
* Implement early design quality practices to mitigate manufacturing issues through the lifecycle
* Lead global failure analysis and corrective action processes to maintain product quality

**Qualifications**

* 10+ years of leadership experience in hardware manufacturing operations, NPI, and quality engineering in high-tech industries
* Direct experience establishing and scaling overseas manufacturing facilities, particularly in Asia
* Deep understanding of electrical fabrication and mechanical processes
* Expertise in advanced quality methodologies such as Six Sigma and Lean Manufacturing
* Bachelor's degree in a technical field; an MS or MBA is a plus

**Benefits**

* 100% premium coverage for Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance
* Equity options available in the form of stock options
* 401(k) match to support retirement savings
* Reimbursement for work-from-home hardware expenses

Our client is an equal opportunity employer. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every qualification—your background could be exactly what this team needs.

card.description:
About PopUp Bagels

 

PopUp Bagels is not just a bagel company—we’re a cultural movement. Our stores are small, our vibes are loud, and our energy is contagious. From signature neon and iconic bullhorns to our “Not Famous but Known” mirror, we’ve reimagined not just how a bagel is created, but how it’s enjoyed: Grip, Rip and Dip! With a cult-like following, massive social presence, and unparalleled collaborations with top companies, partners and Brand Ambassadors PopUp Bagels is defining a new food lifestyle brand.

 

We keep things simple, but we do them really, really well. And our customers agree.

 

The Role

 

We're looking for a Regional Director to lead operations at our Nevada cream cheese production facility. This facility will play an important role in supporting PopUp's continued growth and our ability to deliver the products our customers love.

 

This is a senior operational leadership role responsible for overseeing the day-to-day performance of the facility, from the moment raw materials come through the door to the second finished goods ship out to shops around the country.

 

Here's what makes this role different from other operations roles: we're building something big, and we're building quickly. With established production facilities and operating procedures already in place, the right person for this role will know how to take proven processes, put them into practice, and continue improving them as we grow.

 

We're looking for a problem-solver who isn't afraid to roll up their sleeves and find solutions, a leader who earns trust on the floor just as easily as they collaborate with senior leadership, and someone who can translate operational expectations into consistent, measurable results.

 

This role serves as a key connection between the Nevada production facility and our broader operations leadership team. You'll have the opportunity to influence how we operate, develop our people, and contribute to the continued evolution of our production processes as PopUp expands.

 

If you're a driven leader who thrives in fast-moving environments, values collaboration, and takes pride in building strong teams and efficient operations, this could be the role for you.

 

What You'll Do:

 

Run the Facility. You'll provide day-to-day operational leadership and oversight across Cream Cheese and Schmear production, Warehouse, Quality Assurance, Sanitation, and Equipment Maintenance Working closely with the President of Operations and other facility leaders, you'll implement and maintain established SOPs, manage production schedules, drive throughput targets, and identify opportunities to continuously improve how we operate. You'll be responsible for addressing operational challenges, escalating significant issues when appropriate, and ensuring the facility consistently meets established performance, quality, and safety expectations.

 

Lead People Who Make an Impact. Building a strong team culture is at the core of this role. You'll recruit, develop, and retain a workforce that makes a genuine impact at PopUp Bagels. You'll coach and support your management team, reinforce established training programs, and identify opportunities to strengthen employee development as the operation grows. You'll create an environment where accountability and recognition go hand in hand. Our hourly workforce is the backbone of this operation, and how you show up for them defines everything.

 

Manage the Numbers. You'll be accountable for facility-level operational performance, including production costs, labor efficiency, waste reduction, and budget adherence. You'll partner closely with the President of Operations, Finance, and Accounting on budgeting, forecasting, and period-end reporting, and regularly communicate facility performance, challenges, and opportunities to senior leadership. You'll identify ways to improve efficiency and control costs without compromising quality, safety, or people, while supporting broader capital planning and investment decisions.

 

Drive Supply Chain Alignment. Work directly with our VP of Supply Chain to align production schedules with material availability. You'll oversee raw material procurement planning, inventory controls, and warehouse operations, ensuring established FIFO and food safety standards are consistently followed. You'll collaborate with Supply Chain and other production facilities to support inventory accuracy, product availability, and efficient distribution.

 

Lead Food Safety & Regulatory Compliance. Champion a food-safety-first culture across every part of the facility. You'll ensure consistent execution of established food safety programs and compliance with applicable FDA regulations, FSMA requirements, HACCP plans, and third-party audit standards (SQF, BRC), as applicable. You'll partner with Quality Assurance and the President of Operations to maintain rigorous in-process and finished product quality standards, address compliance concerns, and implement corrective actions when something doesn't meet the bar.

 

Collaborate Across the Company. You'll represent Nevada facility operations in company-wide leadership meetings and collaborate with Distribution & Logistics, Supply Chain, Quality Assurance, and corporate leadership. You'll translate what's happening on the floor into meaningful operational insights, communicate opportunities for improvement, and ensure company priorities and decisions are effectively implemented at the facility level.

 

Who You Are and What You Bring

 

     We're looking for a leader who is genuinely:

 

A scrappy problem-solver. When something breaks at 7am or a key ingredient is backordered, you find a way. You're resourceful, calm under pressure, and put in the time to figure it out. You know when to make decisions, when to collaborate, and when to escalate an issue.

 

A trust-builder. Your team respects you because you've worked to build trust, not because of your title. You're on the floor, you know people's names, and you follow through on what you say.

 

A galvanizing leader. You provide clear direction, get buy-in, and bring your team along with energy and conviction. People want to work hard for you because they know you'll do the same for them.

 

Equally at home in a leadership meeting and a production room. You can review financial and operational performance in the morning and troubleshoot a production issue in the afternoon. You don't ask your team to do what you're not willing to do yourself.

 

Built for growth and continuous improvement. PopUp is growing fast, and our processes will continue to evolve. You appreciate the value of established systems and standards, but you're also comfortable identifying opportunities to make them better. You know how to balance consistency with adaptability as the business scales.

 

       You bring:

 

 
* Bachelor's degree in Food Science, Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent relevant professional experience. Master's degree (MBA or MS) preferred.
 
* 8–10+ years of progressive plant or manufacturing operations leadership experience, including demonstrated responsibility for facility performance, team leadership, and operational budgets.
 
* Experience leading operations in fast-paced manufacturing environments, preferably within growing or multi-site organizations.
 
* Proven track record of leading high-performing, cross-functional manufacturing teams.
 
* Prior food and beverage industry experience strongly preferred; dairy, cream cheese, spreads, or related refrigerated food production experience is a significant plus.
 
* Familiarity with food safety regulatory frameworks, including FSMA, HACCP, GMP, and third-party audit standards (SQF, BRC, AIB).
 
* Strong financial acumen, including budget management, cost analysis, labor efficiency, and operational performance reporting.
 
* Working knowledge of production cost drivers, manufacturing KPIs, and continuous improvement methodologies (Lean, Production Excellence, or equivalent).
 
* Demonstrated experience implementing and maintaining standardized operating procedures, production processes, and operational controls.
 
* Experience partnering with corporate Finance, Supply Chain, Quality Assurance, and Distribution teams.
 
* Availability and willingness to be on-call on weekends and off-hours to respond to facility disruptions or emergencies.
 
* Experience supporting capital improvement projects and operational efficiency initiatives.
 
* A history of building positive, rewarding workplace cultures for hourly workforces.
 

 

Physical Requirements

 

The following physical requirements are representative of those needed to perform the essential functions of this role. Reasonable accommodations may be made for individuals with qualifying disabilities.

 

 
* Ability to walk, stand, and move throughout a production facility for extended periods during daily floor presence and inspections.
 
* Must be able to work in a manufacturing environment with varying temperatures, including refrigerated dairy production and storage areas, moderate to loud noise levels, and exposure to dairy ingredients and food-grade cleaning agents.
 
* Occasional lifting of up to 50 pounds may be required.
 
* Must be able to wear required PPE, including hair nets, beard nets, gloves, and safety footwear when on the production floor.
 
* Ability to use standard office equipment (computer, monitor, phone, conferencing technology) for extended periods.
 
* Occasional travel to corporate offices, other production facilities, or external meetings (estimated up to 30%).
 

 

PopUp Bagels is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.

 

We do not discriminate based on race, age, ancestry, creed, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, pregnancy, childbirth or related condition, unemployment status, gender identity or expression, transgender status, marital status, domestic violence or sexual violence victim status, national origin, citizenship, disability, covered veteran and/or military status, genetic information, familial status, or any other characteristic protected under applicable federal, state, and local law. PopUp Bagels conducts pre-employment screenings in compliance with local, state, and federal laws, and utilizes E-Verify to confirm U.S. employment eligibility.

 

The duties of this position may change from time to time. PopUp Bagels reserves the right to add or delete duties and responsibilities at its discretion. This posting describes the general nature and level of work expected and is not intended to be all-inclusive.

**Job Description**
Be part of the global Integrated Supply Chain (ISC) Engineering leadership team driving factory improvements, product improvements for producibility and cost savings, manufacturing technology implementation, and new product development for Honeywell Aerospace.
 
 
We are hiring a Sr Director to lead the global ISC Advanced Manufacturing Engineering (AME) team for New Product Introduction (NPI) supporting programs across the Aerospace portfolio.
 
 
In this role, you will leverage your extensive product development experience and leadership skills. You will drive continuous improvement to develop new products, processes, and standards in support of the organization's business strategies with a direct impact on development program success. You will develop strategy, hold teams accountable and deliver high impact business results.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Deliver NPI program objectives including product producibility, design-to-cost (DTC) targets, production readiness, and customer quality.
* Operate as a change agent to embed producibility into our core design processes.
* Build Employee Engagement and Skills through the development of standard work, clear roles and responsibilities, and effective training programs.
* Design and develop Management Operating Systems to ensure effective team operations, driving results to program and department objectives.
* Work closely with the SBU engineering team, Program Management, and ISC leaders to build cross-organizational alignment

**Qualifications**
**YOU MUST HAVE**

* Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in a technical discipline such as the sciences, technology, engineering or mathematics
* 8 years of experience in New Product Development
* Knowledge of manufacturing processes
* Experience working with suppliers on technical issues
* Track record of managing multiple projects with demonstrated results on a macro scale
* Experience leading a team with direct line reporting responsibility
* Abitlity to travel 30%

**Us Person Requirements**
Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. Person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status or have the ability to obtain an export authorization.
 
 
**WE VALUE**

* Advanced degree in engineering or business
* Exceptional data analysis and communication skills
* Willingness to raise standards each year to drive organizational excellence
* Ability to make sound and timely judgments in ambiguous environment
* Ability to convey subtle or complex messages clearly, as appropriate for the topic and audience.
* Diverse and global teaming and collaboration
* Balance between demand and capacity when establishing priorities for the organization.

**For Mn Candidates**
The annual base salary range for this position is $238,000-$297,000. Please note that this salary information serves as a general guideline. Honeywell considers various factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate's work experience, education and training, key skills, as well as market and business considerations.
 
 
This position is incentive eligible.
 
 
**Benefits**
Beyond a performance-driven salary, you'll work alongside dedicated experts on technology that's advancing aviation. As a Honeywell Aerospace employee, you're eligible for a comprehensive benefits package that includes:
 
 

* Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision and life insurance
* Short-term and long-term disability coverage
* 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts and health savings accounts
* Employee assistance program and educational assistance
* Parental leave and 12 paid holidays
* Paid time off for vacation, personal and sick time

Explore your benefits: https://honeywellaerospacebenefits.com/
 
 
**POSTING TIMELINE**
The application period for the job is estimated to be 40 days from the job posting date; however, this may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates.

card.title: Director of Quality Control
card.description:
Direct Biologics is a market leading innovator and science-based cGMP manufacturer of regenerative biologic products. Direct Biologics is hiring a hands-on QC leader for our Poway, CA testing laboratory in the greater San Diego area. You will lead a team of analysts to execute release and stability testing for a late-stage extracellular vesicle biologics program as part of a broader multi-product pipeline, and prepare the QC function for commercial operations.

We are currently looking for a Director of QC, responsible for:

* Responsible for strategy and execution of late-stage to commercial cGMP testing laboratory readiness, owning key decisions in method transfer, validation, and life-cycle management.
* Drives phase-appropriate regulatory and compliance initiatives for a portfolio of cell therapy extracellular vesicle products (early clinical through commercial stages). Presents plans to senior leadership and leads QC workstream for inspection readiness.
* Leads interactions with health authorities related to internal and outsource testing programs, including in-process, characterization, drug substance and drug product release, and stability.
* This working leadership position requires hands-on participation in routine and non-routine testing activities. The individual must maintain their own training and qualification, work independently at the laboratory bench, execute test methods, troubleshoot problems, perform investigations, and write reports when needed to meet business and regulatory commitments.
* Collaborates with R&D and Analytical Development team to introduce method lifecycle improvements and new technologies to the QC laboratory.
* Accountable for timely execution and documentation of routine laboratory tests. Ensures the on-time closure of sampling plans, protocols, laboratory investigations, CAPAs, change control records, and other QMS commitments.
* Develops and communicates departmental resourcing plans to serve broad company goals, including personnel, budget, and timelines. Adjusts plans and priorities according to executive leadership resourcing decisions.
* Leads Quality Control operations:
* + Hire, onboard, train, qualify, and assist professional development of QC team members.
* + Ensure timely execution of STAT and release testing.
* + Manage stability sample inventory and pull schedule, coordinating sample transit with cGMP warehouse, outsource sample submission, and timely internal testing.
* + Ensure timely purchase and qualification of supplies, materials, and equipment.
* + Maintain equipment use, calibration, maintenance, and cleaning records and coordinate related activities.
* + Communicate testing timeframes, expected start/finish dates, and testing outcomes to internal and external stakeholders.
* + Author/approve policies, procedures, and work instructions for accuracy and compliance.
* + Author/approve ROA, COA, trend reports, and stability reports.
* Responsible for QC data/records to ensure content adheres to established cGMP quality standards.
* + Maintain risk register, support internal and mock audits, and show steady compliance progress in collaboration with QA team members.
* + Collaborate with IT to ensure data Integrity and storage of original source data in accordance with part 11 requirements.
* Ensure strict adherence to EPA, OSHA, and FAA safety and clean environmental guidelines.
* Occasional travel by air and/or car may be required to participate in on-site vendor activities, such as method transfer, vendor meetings, and vendor quality audits.
* Excels in a fast-paced environment. Independently prioritizes activity based on importance and urgency, manages time well, anticipates challenges, and delivers progress in line with program goals.
* Strong attention to detail and related understanding of CFR, compendial, and other regulatory requirements.

 
 
**Requirements**

**Skill Requirements:**

* Top expert in preparing cGMP clinical stage testing laboratories for commercial launch, with evidence of leading a QC readiness workstream for a late-stage or commercial biologic product.

card.title: Sr. Director, Process Engineering
card.description:
R3 Lithium operates North America's first commercial scale lithium carbonate recovery facility, located in Covington, Georgia. Using a lithium-first extraction process, the company recovers, refines, and returns lithium carbonate from recycled black mass into the battery supply chain for energy storage systems, defense applications, and electric vehicles. Founded in 2026 and privately held, R3 Lithium is headquartered at 9176 Industrial Drive NE, Covington, Georgia. For more information, visit www.r3lithium.com

R3 Lithium is seeking a highly experienced **Lead Discipline Process Engineer** to provide technical leadership for process design, process optimization, and operational excellence across lithium processing and manufacturing operations. This position serves as the subject matter expert for process engineering and is responsible for leading process design activities, supporting project execution, troubleshooting operational challenges, and driving continuous improvement initiatives that enhance safety, reliability, quality, and production performance.

The successful candidate will play a key leadership role in the development, commissioning, and optimization of lithium processing facilities while collaborating with multidisciplinary engineering, operations, maintenance, and project teams.

**Required Qualifications**

**Education**

* Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, Metallurgical Engineering, Process Engineering, or related engineering discipline required.
* Master's degree preferred.

**Experience**

* Minimum **15+ years of progressively responsible process engineering experience** in lithium, chemical processing, mining, hydrometallurgical, battery materials, refining, or industrial manufacturing environments.
* Demonstrated experience leading process engineering activities for large capital projects and operating facilities.
* Experience supporting facility commissioning, start-up, troubleshooting, and process optimization.
* Strong understanding of process simulation, process control, mass and energy balances, and industrial process design.
* Proven leadership experience mentoring engineers and leading multidisciplinary technical teams.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

**Process Engineering Leadership**

* Serve as the technical lead and discipline authority for all process engineering activities.
* Develop and oversee process engineering standards, specifications, and best practices.
* Provide technical leadership and mentorship to process engineers and project teams.
* Review and approve engineering deliverables to ensure technical accuracy and compliance with design requirements.

**Process Design & Project Execution**

* Lead process design efforts including:
* + Process Flow Diagrams (PFDs)
 + Piping and Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs)
 + Heat and Material Balances
 + Equipment Sizing and Specification
 + Process Control Philosophies
 + Process Hazard Analyses (PHA/HAZOP)
* Support feasibility studies, front-end engineering design (FEED), detailed engineering, commissioning, and startup activities.
* Participate in technology evaluations, vendor selection, and equipment procurement activities.
* Support capital project planning, budgeting, scheduling, and execution.

**Process Optimization & Operational Excellence**

* Identify and implement opportunities to improve production efficiency, recovery rates, throughput, product quality, and operating costs.
* Lead root cause investigations and corrective action programs for process-related issues.
* Utilize process data analytics to drive continuous improvement and operational excellence initiatives.
* Develop performance metrics and monitor process key performance indicators (KPIs).

**Safety, Environmental & Regulatory Compliance**

* Ensure process designs and operating practices comply with applicable safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements.
* Lead participation in HAZOP studies, Management of Change (MOC), and risk assessments.
* Promote a strong safety culture and operational discipline throughout the organization.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with lithium extraction, lithium conversion, lithium salts production, hydrometallurgical processing, or battery materials manufacturing.
* Experience with Aspen HYSYS, Aspen Plus, MATLAB, or other process modeling software.
* Professional Engineer (PE) license preferred.
* Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification preferred.
* Experience supporting greenfield facility development and startup activities.

**Core Competencies**

* Process Design & Engineering
* Hydrometallurgical Processing
* Chemical Plant Operations
* Process Simulation & Modeling
* Capital Project Execution
* Process Safety Management (PSM)
* Root Cause Analysis
* Commissioning & Startup
* Continuous Improvement
* Team Leadership & Mentorship
* Technical Risk Assessment
* Cross-Functional Collaboration

**Key Performance Indicators**

* Plant Throughput & Capacity Utilization
* Process Recovery Rates
* Yield Improvement
* Operating Cost Reduction
* Process Reliability & Uptime
* Safety Performance Metrics
* Environmental Compliance
* Successful Capital Project Delivery
* Process Improvement Savings
* Engineering Quality and Execution

card.title: Director of Quality and Accreditation
card.description:
Overview:

**Valley Behavioral Health** is seeking an experienced **Director of Quality and Accreditation** to join our team!

Offering the highest quality of treatment in the area, **Valley Behavioral Health** focuses on providing their patients with the tools and knowledge needed to live happy, healthy lives. Regardless of the level of care, patients receive personalized treatment by a multi-disciplinary team of therapists, social workers, psychiatrists, psychiatric nurses, and other caring mental health professionals.

We are seeking a dynamic and experienced **Director of Quality and Accreditation** to lead our facility’s efforts in ensuring the highest standards of patient care and safety. This leadership role is responsible for overseeing regulatory compliance, quality assurance programs, and continuous improvement initiatives across all clinical and operational areas. The Director will guide the development and implementation of quality protocols, manage accreditation processes, and lead the Quality Assurance and Process Improvement (QAPI) program. The ideal candidate will be a proactive, strategic thinker with a strong commitment to achieving excellence in care delivery and regulatory readiness.

**PURPOSE STATEMENT:**

The Director of Quality and Accreditation is responsible for ensuring patient safety and superior quality of care as measured by survey readiness, treatment program fidelity, and compliance with state and federal laws and regulations and accreditation standards. As such, the Director is responsible for leading and overseeing all aspects of policy development; comprehensive implementation of Acadia’s prescribed clinical protocols, operational quality oversight standards, and programmatic expectations; critical incident reporting; regulatory engagement, including development and submission of plans of correction; certification achievement and maintenance; oversight of the quality assurance and process improvement (QAPI) program; and on-going regulatory readiness strategies at the facility. Through routine physical presence in patient care areas, data analysis and documentation monitoring, and intentional sharing of deep subject-matter expertise, the Director will ensure a proactive, multidisciplinary focus on quality and excellence within the facility.

Responsibilities:

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* Lead and monitor day-to-day regulatory readiness, patient safety, and service excellence across the facility.
* QAPI program oversight and management – follow and develop processes for identification, collection, and analysis of quality performance data.
 + Utilize collected data regarding the outcome of activities for delivering continuously improving services.
 + Conduct annual preparation and evaluation of the facility QAPI Program.
 + Complete process improvement projects and incorporate the results into patient care improvements.
 + Submit quality scorecard data to Acadia corporate office as requested.
 + Coordinate the abstraction of clinical data according to Joint Commission specifications and data entry via vendor database for Inpatient Psychiatric Core Measures (ex. national quality measures such as HBIPS).
 + Identify key aspects of care relevant indicators and evaluation of data using formal and informal feedback from consumers of services and other collateral sources is aggregated and used to improve management strategies and service delivery practices.
 + Lead/coordinate data collection and analysis from all departments within the facility.
 + Prepare and present program data trends and action plans to the monthly Quality Council and quarterly to the Medical Executive Committee and the Governing Board.
* Regulatory preparedness – implement sustainable survey preparation and ongoing monitoring processes, including facility-wide auditing and early-issue identification, to maximize achievement of zero- or standard-level survey outcomes.
 + Facility-wide support – collaborate with other departments to sustainably implement best-practices in regulatory/accreditation compliance as evidenced by measurable results with regard to survey outcomes, patient safety metrics, patient experience results, HBIPS, etc.
 + Develop and maintain proficiency in regulatory planning strategy for all standards for all relevant regulatory and accrediting bodies at the local, state, and federal level.
 + Develop and maintain proficiency in the functionality and auditing within electronic platforms such as electronic patient observations and the electronic medical record, as applicable.
 + Lead Root-Cause Analyses and conduct timely and regular evaluation of serious incidents, complaints, grievances and related investigations to:
 - Identification of events, trends and patterns that may affect client health, safety and or treatment efficacy,
 - Committee evaluation findings and recommendations submitted to agency management for corrective action,
 - Implemented actions, outcomes, trends analyzed over time
 + Develop corrective action plans for the resolution of areas of regulatory vulnerability or those which could compromise patient safety in collaboration with other facility leaders.
 + Ensure proper reporting of violations or potential violations to duly authorized enforcement agencies as appropriate and/or required.
 + Ensure proper reporting of incidents and adverse clinical outcomes to duly authorized enforcement agencies or regulatory agencies as appropriate and/or required.
 + In conjunction with assigned corporate Division Quality Director, initiate and lead communications with regulatory agencies as appropriate.
 + Develop sustainable performance improvement practices through analysis of data and prioritization of efforts to improve survey readiness and consistency of care delivery using expected best-practices.
 + Ensure multidisciplinary ownership of best-practices in self-monitoring, auditing, and process improvement, escalating opportunities for improved engagement to the facility CEO as appropriate.
 + Ensures strategic and operational implementation of regulatory requirements, guidelines, and standards of federal, state, and local licensing agencies, accrediting and certifying organizations.
 + Collaborates with Division and Corporate entities and external parties to ensure strategic quality and patient safety initiatives are fully executed at the facility level. Facilitates effective communication with facility and division leadership regarding key clinical performance improvement activities and initiatives.
 + Serves as a technical advisor, educator and internal consultant to all hospital management, staff, and physicians on the use of performance improvement tools and techniques, analytical techniques, and statistical applications.
 + Ensure facility compliance with policies and applicable standards as required by regulatory/accrediting bodies.
 + Facility leader and subject matter expert on high reliability principles and strategies to achieve zero harm.

* Clinical program excellence – assess fidelity and identify root-causes for gaps/lapses in fidelity to Acadia standards. Support other departments in developing and implementing remediation and improvement plans to achieve fidelity to Acadia’s expected practices, including all elements of treatment program implementation.
* + Develop, review, and educate on internal clinical procedures and appropriate use of outcome evaluation tools and the associated results – including patient experience data and other quality scorecard metrics – to ensure continuous quality improvement and ongoing compliance with federal, state, and third-party regulatory requirements.
 + Translate standards, requirements, and policies into terms or processes meaningful to the facility.
* Leadership – serve as a visible, engaged, and dynamic member of the facility leadership team.
 + Chairs the monthly Quality Council
 + Complete safety rounds, participate in leadership rounding, and submit results/corrective actions to Acadia corporate office.
 + Review incident/safety concerns with the leadership team to identify systemic issues and facilitate the development of corrective actions.
 + Lead and facilitate Root Cause Analyses into all serious and/or sentinel events.
 + Invest in the facility staff through engagement in hiring, development, training, performance management, and communication to ensure effective and efficient operations.
 + Oversees the Culture of Safety Survey and follow-up action planning and sustainment processes.
 + Identification of problems or potential problems to prevent risks to patients and staff. Proposes corrective steps that may include, but are not limited to:
 - Changes in policies/procedures,
 - Staffing and assignment changes,
 - Additional education or training for staff,
 - Addition or deletion of services

**OTHER FUNCTIONS:**

* Perform other functions and tasks as assigned.

Qualifications:

**EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE/SKILL REQUIREMENTS:**

* Bachelor’s Degree in Human Services or nursing required. Master’s degree in behavioral health/risk discipline, Registered Nurse preferred.
* Two or more years of experience in a Quality, Clinical, or PI role required.
* One or more years of management experience preferred.
* Experience with CARF, DEA, Joint Commission, or CMS surveys, as required by service line(s) supported

**LICENSES/DESIGNATIONS/CERTIFICATIONS:**

* Current licensure appropriate for the degree held required.
* CPR and de-escalation/restraint certification required (training available upon hire and offered by facility).
* First aid may be required based on state or facility.

**ADDITIONAL REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS:**

***(******e.g.*** ***emergencies, changes in workload, rush jobs or technological developments) dictate.***
